details: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran indefinitely, effective August 19, 2026. This significant escalation follows alleged ballistic missile launches from Iranian territory towards the Gulf, reportedly targeting maritime traffic. This move further isolates Iran economically, potentially impacting global energy markets due to the region's crucial role in oil trade and Iran's position within it.
title: UAE Imposes Indefinite Trade Embargo on Iran Amid Missile Allegations

details: On August 19, 2026, President Donald Trump hosted a White House summit with leading cryptocurrency and traditional finance executives, alongside the chairs of the SEC and CFTC. The meeting aimed to garner support for and accelerate the passage of a "fair version" of the CLARITY Act, a bill currently stalled in the Senate. This initiative signals the administration's commitment to fostering the U.S. as a leader in the global crypto economy and ending what President Trump termed the "war on crypto." The SEC also reportedly proposed new rules regarding crypto token offerings during the summit.
title: Trump Hosts Crypto Executives to Push CLARITY Act

details: Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit has filed a civil lawsuit against the North Korean government and its Reconnaissance General Bureau (intelligence agency) for a massive $1.5 billion crypto theft that occurred in February 2025. A U.S. federal court has issued a preliminary injunction, freezing some of the stolen funds. This unprecedented legal action highlights the ongoing threat of state-sponsored hacking in the crypto space and the industry's proactive measures to recover illicitly obtained assets.
title: Bybit Sues North Korea for $1.5 Billion Crypto Theft

details: On August 20, 2026, the U.S. Treasury announced it would at least double its long-dated bond buyback operations to a minimum of $4 billion per operation, aiming to provide liquidity and stabilize the bond market. This decision comes as the ongoing Middle East conflict (Iran war) continues to exert upward pressure on oil prices, fueling inflation and complicating the Federal Reserve's monetary policy. The volatility in bond markets and the broader economic implications of the conflict contribute to a cautious financial outlook.
title: US Treasury Doubles Bond Buybacks Amid Iran War's Inflationary Pressure
